category_title: Students who use overprotectiveness and aggression to control partners
scenario_title: Reflective interview on relationship triggers and controlling behavior
minimal_context: The student is participating in a one-on-one interview session with a researcher to discuss relationship behaviors.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Welcome to our first interview session. Today we are going to reflect on your relationship behaviors and how you handle situations with your partner.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I feel [deep sigh] it's not my place; I feel overprotective sometimes. The problem is she doesn't like males touching her, so I feel it's my responsibility to sort out the problems that she's having.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Can you explain what that means for you?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: [Shuffling in chair] Because if I don't do it nothing will get done [pause] the problem keeps going on and on and on. I like to protect my girlfriend (pause) which I have been controlling, sir. It makes me feel as though she needs me, sir. Like I'm wanted.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What happens when you see her interacting with other guys, for example, if you think she is flirting?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: She gives them a special look that she only gives to me! At my previous school, my partners always cheated on me. I snap and lose control... You know, get mad, get angry, usually go outside and bang doors.

dialogue_combined:

STUDENT: I feel [deep sigh] it's not my place; I feel overprotective sometimes. The problem is she doesn't like males touching her, so I feel it's my responsibility to sort out the problems that she's having.

TUTOR: Can you explain what that means for you?

STUDENT: [Shuffling in chair] Because if I don't do it nothing will get done [pause] the problem keeps going on and on and on. I like to protect my girlfriend (pause) which I have been controlling, sir. It makes me feel as though she needs me, sir. Like I'm wanted.

TUTOR: What happens when you see her interacting with other guys, for example, if you think she is flirting?

STUDENT: She gives them a special look that she only gives to me! At my previous school, my partners always cheated on me. I snap and lose control... You know, get mad, get angry, usually go outside and bang doors.

task.content: Participating in the first of 12 weekly one-hour semi-structured case study interviews addressing challenging behavior and intimate violence with the researcher.
task.learning_goal: To address challenging behavior and intimate violence, and prepare students to engage non-defensively.

context.materials: Anonymized instances of challenging behaviors taken from curriculum and extended curriculum database sources
context.time_context: First of 12 weekly one-hour semi-structured case study interviews

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When discussing his interpretation of his partner's facial expressions, specifically when he sees her giving a 'special look' to other guys.
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Snaps and loses control, gets mad, gets angry, usually goes outside and bangs doors.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Jealousy, comparing himself to these guys, and fear that his current girlfriend will cheat on him because partners at his previous school always cheated on him.
related_quotes: You know, get mad, get angry, usually go outside and bang doors
At my previous school, my partners always cheated on me

behavior_patterns.condition: When initially asked to reflect on his intimate violence and instances of challenging behavior.
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Variable defensive responses that entailed positioning to avoid; for example, suggesting current partner had an issue with males touching her when, in fact, it made him uncomfortable.
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Unclear about how latent issues stemming from physical and emotional abuse experienced as a child and subsequent placement in foster care contributed to problem saturated relationship narratives.
related_quotes: I feel [deep sigh] it ’s not my place; I feel overprotective sometimes

behavior_patterns.condition: When explaining his rationale for intervening in his partner's social interactions and taking control.
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Shuffling in chair, pausing, and admitting to controlling behavior.
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Feels it's his responsibility to sort out the problems she's having, feels good because she's trusting him with information, and feels as though she needs him and he is wanted.
related_quotes: Because if I don ’t do it nothing will get done [pause] the problem keeps going on and on and on
It makes me feel good ‘cause it makes me feel as though she ’s trusting me with information
I like to protect my girlfriend (pause) which I have been controlling, sir
It makes me feel as though she needs me, sir. Like I ’m wanted
